A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynFlowNet. All 14 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, figures, tables and equations, support comparison despite substantial expansion and retitling.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecule-generation experiments, property and diversity measurements, retrosynthesis evaluations and reward-proxy analyses (Figures 2–5 and Appendix A).

after.justification: v2 reports original baseline comparisons, backward-policy experiments, scaling studies and fragment-guided generation analyses (Sections 4.1–4.6 and Appendix B). Previously published experimental structures provide inputs to these computational evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 trains forward and backward policies through trajectory balance. v2 introduces separate maximum-likelihood and REINFORCE backward-policy objectives, including replay and reversibility constraints, and replaces learned building-block output weights with fixed fingerprint representations. It also introduces target-informed building-block selection (Sections 3.2–3.3, 4.6 and Appendix A.4).

E1.justification: Coverage expands beyond sEH to GSK3β, DRD2, Mpro and HSP90, and adds recovery of synthesis routes for previously unseen reachable molecules. The earlier ZINC250k and high-affinity ChEMBL property-control comparisons disappear; ChEMBL instead serves as a novelty reference in v2.

E2.justification: The retained fragment-GFlowNet comparison adds FragGFN SA. v2 also evaluates Soft Q-learning, REINVENT4 and SyntheMol, substantially expanding the comparator families. v1's standalone random-trajectory quality comparison in Figure A.4 is no longer reported.

E3.justification: The default building-block count changes from 6,000 to 10,000, and the reported template count from 71 to 105 after preprocessing. Typical sEH training changes from 1,000 steps with beta 64 to 5,000 with beta 32, with revised trajectory limits. Evaluation changes from 1,600 molecules to 1,000 random samples, and AiZynthFinder selection changes from the top 100 to 100 random samples. Mode-count and novelty metrics are added, while SCScore and ligand-efficiency evaluation disappear.

E4.justification: v2 adds backward-policy and entropy ablations, fingerprint-selection comparisons, building-block scaling and cluster/runtime analyses, and fragment-curation and docking-pose case studies (Table 1, Figures 7–8 and Appendix B). Trajectory-length analysis changes scope. v1's reward-exponent sensitivity and proxy-versus-IC50 correlation/ROC analyses are removed.

E5.justification: v1 presents molecule-level distributions and point summaries without declared repeated-run counts or cross-seed uncertainty. v2 reports standard errors from three training seeds in Table A.2, three seeds for Figure 7, and eight seeds for Figure A.3. This establishes substantially expanded statistical reporting, without establishing how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the main comparison results and adds substantial baseline, target, backward-policy and scaling outcomes. For example, v1 reports 47% AiZynthFinder success (Table A.3); v2 reports 40% for L=4 and 62% for L=3 in Figure 4, but 65% for L=3 in Table A.2. Changed settings prevent interpreting these as direct gains. Table 1 newly reports 32.3% and 44.3% unseen-route recovery for maximum-likelihood and REINFORCE policies, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal backward-training objectives (Equations 2–3) and a short constant-reward state-count argument, without developing new theorems or proofs. These are limited mathematical additions beyond v1's framework description. The REINFORCE specification is internally inconsistent: Section 3.2 describes maximization, while Algorithm 2 specifies minimization.

C1.justification: The synthesis-aware generation claim remains, but v2's main contributions expand to backward-policy learning, large-action-space scaling, novelty against stronger baselines and experimental-fragment-guided design. v1's explicit claim of comparability to bioactive ChEMBL compounds and its 'first application' conclusion are dropped. The title also shifts from guaranteed synthesis pathways to synthesis constraints.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of backward-flow leakage, fingerprint-driven cluster exploitation and baseline novelty differences, plus qualifications about molecule-size effects and docking's omission of water-mediated interactions. It removes v1's explicit discussion of reward-proxy generalization uncertainty, uncertain laboratory yields and the proxy-versus-experimental-activity validation (v1 Limitations; v2 Sections 3.2, 4.1–4.5 and Appendix B.3).

D1.justification: Beyond v1's basic model and training table, v2 documents reaction preprocessing, backward-training algorithms and replay, baseline training budgets and hyperparameters, clustering tools, docking preparation and fragment-curation procedures (Appendices A–B). These substantially expand reproducibility information. The SynFlowNet source-code link itself is retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially, especially through a dedicated backward-policy discussion positioning the approach against Jang et al. and Mohammadpour et al. v2 also acknowledges concurrent RGFN work by Koziarski et al., qualifying the earlier first-application positioning, and broadens discussion of synthesis-aware generation and modern comparison methods (Section 2).

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background becomes a separate section with four subsections; methods and results are reorganized around distinct research questions. The appendix is restructured into Extended Methods and Extended Results. Some original action-space and network descriptions remain or move, but the overall narrative is substantially revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn to explain fingerprint sampling and backward-policy constraints. The earlier boxplot-focused presentation expands into violin plots, mode-discovery and scaling curves, and docking-pose panels. Tables are restructured and algorithm boxes added. Earlier SCScore, ligand-efficiency, proxy-validation and top-50-molecule displays disappear or are replaced with different content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence beyond v1's narrow single-target evaluation through stronger baselines, multiple targets, repeated-seed reporting and direct tests of backward-policy consistency and scaling. It also diagnoses an important previously unexamined MDP problem and documents proposed remedies. Losing v1's proxy validation and laboratory-feasibility caveats, the 62%/65% discrepancy, and conflicting REINFORCE optimization directions weaken the revision, but the broader controlled evidence and methodological detail provide a substantial net quality improvement.
